Proportional abundance with known reference abundances

Source: R/proportional.abundance.R
proportional.abundance.ref_abu.Rd

Computes the proportional abundance of every sample, as proportional.abundance() does, when the reference abundance of every element is already known (e.g. from an external database or a larger collection of samples) instead of being a percentile of the given samples.

Usage

proportional.abundance.ref_abu(abund, ref_abu, cap_at = NULL)

Arguments

abund

Numeric matrix, data.frame or sparse Matrix of abundances with samples in rows and elements (units or subunits) in columns. Column names are the element identifiers.

ref_abu

Numeric vector of strictly positive reference abundances, one per element (column of abund). If named, values are matched to the columns by name (extra names are ignored); otherwise they follow the order of the columns. With cap_at, reference abundances may also be 0: the ratio of such an element is cap_at in the samples where it is present, and 0 where it is absent.

cap_at

NULL (default) or a single positive number. If NULL, the ratios are not capped. Otherwise, every element's ratio higher than cap_at is set to cap_at. With percentile = 100 every ratio is at most 1, so only a cap_at below 1 changes the result.

Value

Named numeric vector with the proportional abundance of every sample. Samples with zero total abundance get 0.

Details

With \(R_j\) the reference abundance of element \(j\), $$PA_i = \sum_{j \,:\, x_{ij} > 0} \frac{x_{ij}}{R_j},$$ or, with a numeric cap_at \(c\), $$PA_i = \sum_{j \,:\, x_{ij} > 0} \min\left(\frac{x_{ij}}{R_j}, c\right).$$

Ratios are not bounded by 1: abundances above their reference give ratios above 1, unless capped. Elements absent from a sample contribute 0 to it.

See also

proportional.abundance()

Examples

abund <- matrix(
  c(10, 0, 4, 6,
    5,  8, 3, 0,
    0, 12, 7, 9),
  nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE,
  dimnames = list(c("S1", "S2", "S3"), c("e1", "e2", "e3", "e4"))
)

# Reference abundances from an external database
proportional.abundance.ref_abu(abund, ref_abu = c(e1 = 8, e2 = 10, e3 = 5, e4 = 12))
#>    S1    S2    S3 
#> 2.550 2.025 3.350 

# Element e4 without reference abundance: its ratio is cap_at where present
proportional.abundance.ref_abu(abund, ref_abu = c(e1 = 8, e2 = 10, e3 = 5, e4 = 0), cap_at = 1)
#>    S1    S2    S3 
#> 2.800 2.025 3.000
